source.title: SALR: Sharpness-Aware Learning Rate Scheduler for Improved Generalization
source.authors: Xubo Yue; Maher Nouiehed; Raed Al Kontar

record.tranche_reason: Compares Adam with SGD on held-out classification accuracy, using the paper’s own benchmark experiments rather than reproducing the optimizer studies cited in the claim.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports CIFAR-10 test accuracy for SGD and Adam. The paper also reports SALR comparisons and sharpness values, but those do not test the specific versions’ stated interventions or magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.test_reason: Table 1 directly compares Adam and SGD test accuracy on four CIFAR-10 networks, bearing on V4. The tuning protocol is insufficiently documented to establish the claim's limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: SALR improves held-out performance across their tested tasks and tends to find flatter solutions at the same total number of gradient calls. Matching gradient calls does not itself establish equal wall-clock runtime.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares Adam and SGD within SALR experiments, but does not reproduce the cited optimizer comparisons or their limited-tuning setup. Experiments use the study’s own training settings and benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice changes which method has higher CIFAR-10 accuracy across the four reported networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 2 and 7 report the paper's sharpness measure alongside test accuracy. Perturbations are not scaled to weight magnitudes, and train-test gaps are not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The paper's local loss-based sharpness measure can accompany differences in held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: SALR improves held-out performance over its base optimizers across the reported classification, text-prediction, and fine-tuning experiments at matched total gradient calls.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scheduling learning rates using local sharpness can improve held-out performance at a matched gradient-call budget.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: The optimizer comparison is reported only for four networks on CIFAR-10 in this section; the paper does not establish that tuning is limited to learning rates and decay schedules. No training accuracies are given for this comparison.
record.rows_left_out: The other Table 1 comparisons concern SALR, SWA, Entropy-SGD and SAM rather than the adaptive-optimizer comparison named by V4. Tables 2–7 report sharpness or other benchmark results, but do not test a version’s specified measure or intervention.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

A verified restriction to learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning; training-performance comparisons; adaptive optimizers other than Adam; language comparisons; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the batch penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with train-test gaps at comparable training loss, and ranking against norm and margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. The small Adam advantages qualify an 'often' claim rather than contradicting a universal prediction. No significance tests or training accuracies accompany the four optimizer comparisons. Other relevant-looking results use different interventions or sharpness measures and were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold is reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison is reported.
No language benchmarks, broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, or Adam-to-SGD switch is tested.
Batch size is not varied to measure a large-batch generalization gap.
Dropout is used at probability 0.5 across methods, but its effect is not tested.
The study does not measure magnitude-scaled weight perturbations or compare that measure’s ranking of train-test gaps.
No memorized training examples are removed.
